related_questions.question: What are the current treatments for COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: Current COVID-19 treatments include antiviral medications and supportive care. Antivirals like Paxlovid, remdesivir, and molnupiravir are authorized for individuals at high risk of severe illness. Supportive care focuses on managing symptoms and may include rest, hydration, and over-the-counter medications.

list.snippet: Paxlovid (nirmatrelvir with ritonavir): An oral antiviral taken at home for adults and children ages 12 and older.
Remdesivir (Veklury): An intravenous antiviral administered at a healthcare facility for 3 days.
Molnupiravir (Lagevrio): An oral antiviral for adults.

text_blocks.snippet: Antiviral medications are typically offered to individuals with mild to moderate symptoms who are at high risk of severe illness, and who have had symptoms for 7 days or less. Factors that can put someone at high risk include older age, certain underlying medical conditions, and being immunocompromised.

list.snippet: Rest and hydration: Getting enough rest and staying hydrated are important for recovery.
Over-the-counter medications: These can help manage symptoms like fever, cough, and aches.

list.title: Consult a doctor:
list.snippet: It's crucial to talk to a doctor to determine the most appropriate treatment plan and to see if you qualify for antiviral medications.

list.title: Early treatment:
list.snippet: Antiviral treatments are most effective when started early in the course of the illness.
